newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends off 150 bps on late demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends off 150 bps on late demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates extended early falls to close down 150 basis points at 21.60 percent on Friday due to late demand for paper, traders said.
"There were those who hung onto paper and others who were desperate to cover positions at low rates," a trader said.
"Even so, the closing rate was settled after two very small deals as the session itself was very dull. We expect to return to around 22.50 percent again on Monday," he added.
Stability in the money and foreign exchange markets led traders to expect rates to fall again at next Tuesday's auction.
"We think rates can still fall, albeit marginally; they may even stay the same."
"The markets have been very calm in recent sessions, and furthermore the long bond yield is low," he added.

The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.9 of a centavo firmer at 7.5270/7.5320 per dollar. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield had fallen to 6.74 percent at the time the Mexican money market closed from 6.84 percent at Thursday's close.
